edges.description: IL-1-driven autoinflammation produces the systemic inflammatory response (fever, arthralgia, bone pain, acute-phase reactant elevation).
IL-1-mediated systemic autoinflammation is associated with the defining chronic urticarial rash.
Systemic IL-1-driven inflammation directly induces recurrent febrile episodes.
Systemic inflammation produces characteristic bone pain.
Systemic inflammatory cytokine release produces frequent arthralgia.
Sustained systemic autoinflammation leads to non-erosive inflammatory arthritis in over half of patients.
Systemic inflammatory flares frequently produce generalized myalgia.
Chronic systemic inflammation drives reactive lymphadenopathy.
Reticuloendothelial activation during chronic systemic inflammation causes hepatomegaly.
Chronic systemic autoinflammation causes persistent constitutional fatigue.
Sustained systemic inflammation and hypercatabolism cause constitutional weight loss.
Systemic autoinflammatory serositis manifests clinically as pericarditis in a subset of patients.
Systemic IL-1-driven inflammation induces hepatic acute-phase synthesis of CRP and elevates ESR.
Clonal B-cell/plasma-cell proliferation secretes monoclonal IgM (most commonly IgM kappa) into the circulation.
Serum acute-phase reactants (CRP, ESR) reflect the IL-1-driven systemic inflammatory response.

nodes.description: Anakinra is a recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist that blocks both IL-1 alpha and IL-1 beta. It is a very effective treatment for Schnitzler syndrome, producing rapid clinical remission, but requires daily subcutaneous injection and symptoms recur shortly after stopping.

evidence.snippet: The interleukin (IL) 1 receptor antagonist anakinra is a very effective treatment, but requires daily injection and blocks both IL-1α and IL-1β.

nodes.description: Canakinumab is a selective human monoclonal anti-IL-1 beta antibody with a long half-life allowing monthly dosing. A randomized placebo-controlled study demonstrated efficacy, with significant improvement in clinical signs, inflammatory markers, and quality of life. It is effective in anakinra-treated patients and is a key targeted therapy.

nodes.description: Schnitzler syndrome is now regarded as an acquired adult-onset autoinflammatory disease in which dysregulated innate immunity drives systemic inflammation. Interleukin-1 (especially IL-1 beta) is the pivotal mediator; the near-pathognomonic response to IL-1 inhibitors demonstrates the central role of this cytokine in disease pathogenesis.

evidence.snippet: Schnitzler syndrome shares strong clinicopathologic similarities with monogenic IL-1-mediated autoinflammatory disorders and is now considered an acquired adult-onset autoinflammatory disease.

nodes.description: A monoclonal IgM (rarely IgG) gammopathy is a mandatory feature of Schnitzler syndrome, reflecting an underlying clonal B-cell/plasma-cell process. The relationship between the monoclonal component and the autoinflammation is not fully understood, but a shared pathophysiologic mechanism is hypothesized, and the clonal process underlies the long-term risk of lymphoproliferative transformation.
